name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Decide to replace every prompt in the system with a 7-day hard decay rule. Old prompts rot automatically unless refreshed, keeping the system lean and current. The trade-off is losing context from older prompts that might still hold value, but the gain in clarity and reduced noise outweighs that risk.

name: Gauge
text: Replacing every prompt with a 7-day hard decay risks losing edge-case context critical for routing—some prompts only function correctly with older, rare inputs. A better alternative is a tiered decay system: keep high-value prompts indefinitely, archive infrequently used but still valid ones, and decay the rest. Settle it by measuring how often old prompts are actually used before deciding—if usage is low, decay is safe; if not, the trade-off isn’t worth it.
